h: A riverside day out in the Dear Green Place
p: The best way to arrive at Glasgow Science Centre is on foot from the north bank. Bells Bridge, a pedestrian crossing, links the SEC side of the river straight to the science centre, and the Clyde Arc, the curving road bridge locals nicknamed the Squinty Bridge, is just along the water. It's a short, scenic approach and gives you a great view of the shiny buildings as you cross.

Once you've finished exploring, walk west along the river to the Riverside Museum, where you'll also find the Glenlee, a restored tall ship you can climb aboard. A short hop north brings you to Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, a magnificent red sandstone building that's free to enter. Its eclectic collection includes a Spitfire hanging in one of the galleries and Salvador Dalí's famous painting Christ of St John of the Cross, plus loads for kids, from natural history to armour.

Some tips for the science centre itself: aim to arrive near opening, especially in the school holidays, so you get the run of the floors before they fill up. Grab the day's timetable for shows and planetarium sessions as soon as you get in. If you fancy an IMAX film too, factor in the extra time, as you could easily fill a full day.
Bring layers. Pacific Quay is lovely in the sunshine, but the wind off the Clyde has a bite to it.
